newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria finmin to issue fixed-interest securities.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria finmin to issue fixed-interest securities.

text.p: Bulgaria's finance ministry will issue more fixed-interest securities, a which reflects expectations of stability after a currency board was launched eleven days ago, Deputy Finance Minister Plamen Oresharski said.
"At this stage, we plan most of our issues to be three-, six- and 12-month fixed-interest government bonds," Oresharski told Reuters.
Currently, the Finance Ministry sustains banks' liquidity through short-term discount treasury bills sold weekly by the ministry.

The fixed-interest bonds will be more attractive for investors because interest rate fluctuations are expected to be minimal since Bulgaria launched an IMF-prescribed fixed-exchange rate regime, or currency board, to stabilise its fragile financial system, he said.
The currency board system anchors the lev to the mark and bans all forms of central bank lending to the government and commercial banks.
Interest rates remain a key instrument in regulating liquidity in the banking system under the currency board system through marketing of government securities and interbank deposits.
Bulgarian interest rates are expected to shadow the interest rates of the anchor currency, or mark in this case, and have an added risk premium, he said.
He saw annual interest rates rising to 10 to 12 percent later this year.
"In cases of liquidity shortages, the risk premium may double," he added.
Interest rates have fallen to 0.58 percent monthly from March's 18 percent, reflecting economic stabilisation following an IMF reform and funding deal reached in March.
"Rates fell in the past months not because of fundamental changes in the Bulgarian economy, but due to excessive lev liquidity and higher demand for long-term paper," said Oresharski.
The central bank cut the annual rate to 6.96 percent from July 14.
The ministry may consider more regular issues of longer-term papers in September, said Oresharski.

"First, we will see how the three-year floating coupon issue we placed this week trades and then probably plan such issues once or twice a month," he added. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
